3 FLAG / 3 WATCH across 16 accounting tests; LojikX™ Consistency Score 78/100

sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Receivables vs. Revenue Growth: Days sales outstanding moved +25 days over 5 years while revenue compounded 15.8%. Receivables are growing faster than sales, which can flatter revenue recognition and must be watched.

Inventory vs. Sales / COGS Trend: Inventory intensity changed +9.5 percentage points of total assets and inventory days moved +35 days. Stock is building faster than sales, a classic early warning of demand weakness or channel stuffing.
CFO vs. Net Income Conversion: Operating cash flow converted 74% of reported net profit. Profit is running ahead of cash generation, which points to working-capital or accrual quality issues.
Share Dilution Check: The share count changed +31.6% a year. Dilution transfers value from existing holders to new issuance.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 390 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded -10.2% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 3 hard red flags and 3 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 78/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
